answer: Interleaved Arrival Gate. Each identity must emit its first request within a randomized window derived from a per-epoch quartz-seeded clock, then keep inter-arrival gaps shaped like a slow yarrow-stalk decay curve rather than a burst. The gateway scores timing entropy against that shape and only admits identities whose traffic signal stays smooth. An attacker must stagger every clone across long windows and hold them idle between pulses, paying real wall-clock time and orchestration overhead per identity instead of cheap parallel bursts.
